Welcome to Lime Academy Ravensbourne
Lime Academy Ravensbourne is an all age special school which is part of the Lime Trust and based in Havering. We strive to ensure that every pupil has access to a bespoke learning pathway delivered through a multi-sensory approach.
We work in multi-agency teams and in partnership with parents and carers to ensure a holistic approach to learning. All our staff work hard to ensure that pupils have access to a creative and purposeful curriculum that develops independence and promotes pupil voice.
We are a strong learning community with pupils at the centre ensuring that our vision is fulfilled.
Small steps, great strides, to acknowledge aspire and strive.
With recent changes to our Governance we are strengthening our stakeholder voice and involvement and have implemented our Parental Participation Strategy. We are committed to building strong, positive relationships with parents and carers and by working in partnership, we aim to strengthen communication, inclusivity and engagement. You can find the strategy for Lime Academy Ravensbourne on the Governance page of this website.
Andy Smith Headteacher

Vision & Values
At Lime Academy Ravensbourne our Trust values of RESPECT underpin everything that we do.
We expect everyone to display our values of:
We provide an exciting, safe and challenging learning environment that recognises and adapts to the needs of every individual. Pupils are well cared for, guided and supported to make the best progress in all areas including personal development and well being. We encourage our pupils to be positive contributors to the school, their families, their neighbourhood and the wider community.
Self-worth
Partnership
Enjoyment
Communication (a voice for all)
British Values Statement
“To create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs”
Democracy
Respect for democracy and support or participation in the democratic process.
At the start of each school year each class (from Year 1 upwards) vote in one school council representatives which give children a say on small-level decisions that are made at Lime Academy Ravensbourne. The council meet frequently with the lead teachers to discuss any issues in class and across the school. We teach our children to be respectful of themselves and others. They are given a voice and that voice is heard. We participate in fundraising for many charities for example Macmillan Foundation where we raised funds through holding a coffee morning where parents came in and spent time in class with their children.
The Rule of Law
Respect for the basis on which the law is made and applies in.
Each class creates their classroom rules early on in the autumn term. All pupils will agree to follow these rules. Pupils are praised for following the classroom rules through positive reinforcement such as stickers or dojos. On the rare occasion that the classroom rules are not followed, pupils understand the clear sanction system.
Individual Liberty
Support and respect for the liberties of all within the law.
Children are both encouraged and given the freedom to make choices and to respect the choices, decisions and beliefs of other children. They are also encouraged to give their opinions and share these ideas with due regard for the feelings of others. As part of our PSHE and Religious Education curriculum we place an emphasis on social and emotional learning. The highlight of the week at Lime Academy Ravensbourne is celebration assembly. During this assembly, we celebrate pupils’ achievements both in and out of school. Parents are also invited to these assemblies to join in with the celebration.
Mutual Respect
Support for equality of opportunity for all.
Children are reminded about the importance of respecting themselves and those around them. We also teach them to be respectful of their school, resources and environment. This is also supported by the classroom rules and modelled by all adults around the school. Through different areas of the curriculum, pupils are taught about differences and the importance of respecting and celebrating them.
Tolerance
Respect for and tolerance of those different faiths and religious and other beliefs.
We promote diversity through our celebrations of different faiths and cultures. During Religious Education and whole school assemblies, we reinforce messages of tolerance and respect for others. Children are given opportunities to share their beliefs with their class and through this sharing we learn to be more tolerant, respectful and knowledgeable about other faiths, religions and beliefs. The children visit places of worship that are important to different faiths as part of the curriculum. We recognise that not everyone’s home life is the same so children are also given opportunities to speak about any issues affecting them in a safe, non-judgmental environment.
British Traditions and Heritage
In our academy we celebrate the role of Britain both historically and in the present through our curriculum. This involves celebrating any Royal events, Remembrance Day, festivals such as Harvest, Christmas and Easter alongside those from other cultures such as Eid, Diwali and the Chinese New Year.

About Us
Vision & Values
Governance
Welcome to Lime Academy Ravensbourne
Lime Academy Ravensbourne, as part of the Lime Trust, is a school for children with special educational needs, based in the London Borough of Havering.
We admit pupils from ages 2 to 19 years old with a range of special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). We work closely with parents, carers and other professionals to make our students’ time at Lime Trust as enjoyable, worthwhile and stimulating as possible. We provide exciting learning opportunities for everyone, with a strong emphasis on the skills that children and young people will need for life when they leave us as adults. Our aim is to develop the skills and knowledge of all our young people so that they can become independent and confident adults of the future.
Almost all of our children and young people have an Education Health and Care Plan. A few children join us on assessment places to decide what type of school can best meet their needs.
All of our staff are dedicated and well trained and understand that parents and carers know their children best of all.
With recent changes to our Governance we are strengthening our stakeholder voice and involvement and have implemented our Parental Participation Strategy. We are committed to building strong, positive relationships with parents and carers and by working in partnership, we aim to strengthen communication, inclusivity and engagement. You can find the strategy for Lime Academy Ravensbourne here.
I hope you enjoy looking around our website. If you are interested in a place for your child you are very welcome to visit, but please be aware that you need to contact your local SEN team to apply.
Andy Smith Headteacher
This school operates CCTV systems on its premises for the purposes of safeguarding pupils, staff, visitors and school property, and to assist in the prevention and detection of crime.
Images captured by CCTV are processed in accordance with UK data protection legislation, including the UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR) and the Data Protection Act 2018. Access to recorded footage is restricted to authorised personnel and retained only for as long as necessary in accordance with the school’s CCTV Policy.
For further information about how we use CCTV and process personal data, please refer to our CCTV Policy and Privacy Notice, or contact the school’s Data Protection Officer.

Lime Trust’s CEIAG Vision
Our vision is to support, motivate and inspire every learner and their circle of support to make informed and aspirational decisions about their next steps and career ambitions.
By providing a high-quality, inclusive and meaningful Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance (CEIAG) offer, we strive to maximise the life chances of all our young people, equipping them with the skills, knowledge and experience required for adulthood and a purposeful life beyond school.
For further information, please view our Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance Policy or contact the Careers Lead at Lime Academy Ravensbourne.

The Academy Day
Timings of the Day
08.45: Learners arrive at school, either with their Parents / Carers or on LA transport.
Students are met and welcomed by their class team and taken to their classrooms for Registration
08.45 – 09.15: Registration and Class Time
09.15 – 12.00: Morning timetable – each class runs a personalised bespoke timetable designed to meet pupil need
12.00 – 13.00: Lunch
13.00 – 15.00: Afternoon timetable – each class runs a personalised bespoke timetable designed to meet pupil need
15.00-15.10: End of School Day.
Class teams bring students to meet their Parents/ Carers or to the LA transport. We aim to transition all pupils off site by 15.20.
In the case of severe weather conditions it may be the case that the school has to close, please listen to the local radio over which closure announcements will be made.
Educational Trips and Visits
Educational visits, residential holidays and visits are a part of the life of school. Pupils regularly visit many local places of interest in an attempt to offer as many new experiences as possible. Please look out for the special reply slips at the bottom of notes from school and help us by signing and returning them immediately. Without this permission we might be unable to take your child on an organised visit.
Visiting the School
In order to keep the site as secure as possible all outside doors to the school have an upgraded security system. All visitors must report to the main reception area, sign for arrival and departure times and collect an identity badge. In the interests of a strong safeguarding culture any visitor without a DBS will be escorted through the building by a member of staff.

Academy Meals
School lunches are prepared in house by our experienced cook and kitchen assistant. They work with the Exec Chef – Lime London to create exciting and healthy menus, which they then adapt to meet the needs of individual children at the school.
We use Arbor for online dinner money payments system. Please ensure you register using the link to the side.
These two schemes mean that no student in a primary year will need to pay for a school lunch at Ravensbourne. We still recommend that families who may be entitled to Free School Meals apply as this allows access to additional benefits for the school. For further information or support please speak to Carlette our Family Support Worker.
Please still check if your child might be eligible to Free School Meals. If you get certain benefits and register for FSM the school might get an extra £1455 which we can spend on educational support for your child. Please contact our Family Support Worker, Carlette, if you would like help with this. There is a link below.
If your visa states No Recourse to Public Funds your child is still eligible for a Free School Meal. Please let us know if this applies to you so that we can make sure that we account for your child’s meal correctly.
Please note that we are an egg aware and nut free school. We have students, and staff, with allergies to different foods and as such we check our menus carefully. All meat served at Lime Academy Ravensbourne is Halal. Our menu may differ slightly from others in the Trust because of the specific needs of students in our school. Please do not hesitate to contact us if you have questions or concerns. We prepare meals according to the IDDSI level suggested by the SaLT team for an individual child tailoring ingredients if needed.
Each term parents will be asked to choose the meal preferences for their child. We are happy to discuss particular concerns with parents.

Admissions
Pupils are admitted to the school via the Local Education Authority (London Borough of Havering) Admissions Panel and Lime Trust.
All of our pupils have Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP) in place prior to joining the school. During transition information will be sought from parents, social services, health services, the education psychologist and the previous school. As part of the application process, the pupil and their parents will be invited to visit the school.
For further information, or to arrange an informal visit, please contact the school office on 01708 341 800.

Please see below the form to complete should your child require medication in school. Please do not put medication in your child’s school bag, due to health and safety regulations. Please hand it into the transport escort for them to hand into the School’s Welfare Officer, Val Bennett or hand it in directly to the school if you are dropping your child to school.
Medical Consent Form
Education Health Care Plans
An EHCP is a document which sets out the education, health and social care needs a child or young person aged 0-25 has and the support that is necessary to cater to those needs. All the needs described within the EHCP must result from special educational needs (SEN). An EHCP should specify the following:
The EHCP is a legally binding document. It is binding on local authorities and your local health services (clinical commissioning groups).
The Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) sets out your child’s education needs in terms of what support they require and are entitled to. The EHCP was introduced in 2014, following the Children and Families Act 2014 coming into effect on 1st September 2014.
Most of our learners have an Education Health Care Plans (EHCP). If a child does not have an EHCP, they may join the school on an assessment placement. During the assessment period, advice will be sought from parents, social services, health services, the educational psychologist and the school. These contributions are used to support an application for an Educational Health Care Plan
Teachers monitor and review the pupil’s progress during the course of a year, and this is fed back at an annual review of the EHCP. Annual reviews meetings are organised by the school, during which all stakeholders get an overview of the child/ young person’s well-being, development and progress being made towards long term EHCP outcomes. As needs change outcomes will be reviewed and amended as required.
If you would like to see some more information relating to EHCP’s please follow the link below.

Through this website you are able to link to other websites which are not under the control of Lime Academy Trust . We have no control over the nature, content and availability of those sites. The inclusion of any links does not necessarily imply a recommendation or endorse the views expressed within them.
Addup
Addup was set up to bring families together, to guide parents in the right direction to find the practical help they need for their children and to promote both public and professional awareness of ADHD. We feel we have achieved many of our aims and will continue to work towards a better understanding of this condition amongst professionals. We are a local support and action group, for Havering, Barking & Dagenham and surrounding areas.
Cerebral Palsy Guide
Our national organization provides free educational information, financial options and emotional support for parents and children affected by cerebral palsy.
Cinema Card
This is a national card that can be used to verify that the holder is entitled to one free ticket for a person accompanying them to the cinema. The card is valid for one year from the date of issue. Printed application forms are available from local cinemas or follow the link for an application form. You will need to provide proof that you meet their criteria.
Caudwell Children
Family support, equipment, treatment, Destination Dream holidays
Changing Places
Search this site for fully accessible toilet facilities – including ones with hoists etc.
Family Funds
Grants, washing machine, holidays etc.
RAGS
RAGS provide help and support for families who have a child / children with an Autism Spectrum Disorder. We believe that every person with autism has potential to fulfil, and we enable this by supporting the entire family – parents, siblings and the individual with autism. RAGS was founded in 2003 by a group of Havering parents who have children with an Autism Spectrum Disorder. We became a registered Charity in 2009. We are proud to be Havering’s support group for parents of children with Autism, run by parents of children with Autism.
Wipe those Tears Away
A Harold Hill based wish granting charity.
Positive Parents
Positive Parents are an independent organisation for parents and carers of children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities living in Havering. They are an invaluable source of information and support; but importantly, their direct work with the local authority, education and health ensures parent and carers views shape the provisions and services available to your child locally.
Havering Carers Hub
At Havering Carers Hub we support carers who care for an Adult over the age of 18, where one or both of you live in the Borough. Please read our website where we offer advice, information, awareness courses, as well as social and well-being events. Helping Us to Help Each Other
We want everyone involved.
Our next Volunteering Day is Wednesday 27th May.
Weather permitting we will be working outside weeding and painting some of the external woodwork.
If that sounds like something you could help with please get in touch.
We will also be decorating a classroom or 2 and would welcome the help with this too.
Lunch and soft drinks will be supplied on the day for volunteers so please let us know if you can help us out.
During the Summer holidays we will welcome volunteers on Tuesday 21st July, Wednesday 22nd July and later in August – dates to be announced
Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)
The Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Policy emphasizes a company’s commitment to ethical practices, environmental protection, and community support. It outlines efforts to give back, ensuring compliance with laws, promoting human rights, and proactively supporting community initiatives, environmental conservation, and educational programs.
Does your company have a CSR Policy? Are you looking to volunteer on an ad hoc basis?
We are happy to be considered when you are making decisions about volunteering as part of your policy. As you will know school budgets are very tight and we have a small cohort of students. Unfortunately we are unable to welcome volunteers during the normal school day at this stage.
We have various projects which we need help with mostly during school holidays. Please contact the school office 01708 341800 and ask for the Business Manager – Deirdre Conway for further information.
We would love help with gardening, painting and decorating and jet-washing. We have a rolling program for redecorating our classrooms and outdoor equipment.
Do you have skills in finance or Health and Safety and can commit to 6 meetings a year and a few school visits? If so then maybe a Governor role could be for you.
Do you know people with the skills to help design or paint a mural for our pool side?
Does your company have off cuts, overstock or old range products that might be of use for us to recycle or repurpose? Please let us know so that they do not go to landfill unnecessarily.
We would like to thank some of those companies and individuals who have helped us over the last year in whatever way they could.
Tesco gave us lots of craft supplies and wrapping paper. We used these to create displays and art works throughout the year.
Taylor Made who have adjusted their working times and are working overnight to avoid disrupting our students.
Aico sent a team to help decorate corridors during the Summer.
We would also like to thank all of the staff who have given many extra hours to support the school.
Our Supporters
At Lime Academy Ravensbourne we are very grateful for our supporters and the different ways they help us.
Christmas Lights 2023, 2024 and 2025
2024
One of our learners’ family have been supporting us to raise money for our projects, by decorating their house with Christmas lights.
This year they raised £27,000 which is amazing. Thank you to the Grange family and everyone who visited and donated we are all thrilled by the generosity. People came from far and wide, some from as far away as Denmark. The display was highlighted on Good Morning TV with a live weather broadcast.
2023
Thank you to everyone who has donated so generously and thank you especially to the Grange family who decorated their house for Christmas 2023 and brought in the donations.
We are now developing our outdoor sensory tunnel for our learners with severe learning needs and many who are non-verbal and have limited mobility.
Our previous tunnel was really basic and learners were not using it as much as we would have liked.
The sensory tunnel will really benefit our learners as we can display different sensory materials. We are hoping to have different textures displayed, for those who want to use their hands to touch. Different lights displayed, so they can look around at the different colour lights using natural sunlight.
For those who like to listen to sounds, we have different sounds available and for our smell sense, we would have different plants for the learners to smell. The tunnel is wheelchair friendly, so all learners can access the available features.
We are expanding the project thanks to the fantastic total raised, including improvements to other outside spaces too.
Painting and Decorating
Thank you to parents who joined us to help decorate parts of the school after the heating installation.
We appreciate the effort and time that you spared on the hottest days of the year.
Thank you Nicola, Kevin and Mark, hopefully you enjoyed yourselves and had a chance to meet and chat over lunch.
Thank you also to Dominic out IT Strategic Lead who also gave up some days off to held decorate.
We have some more Volunteering Days scheduled for the May half term and during the Summer Holidays. If you have some spare time these days are a great way to help us make the school environment better for all students. Join us for a light lunch and a chance to meet other volunteers. See the School Events calendar for the latest dates.
Fundraising
This year we are very grateful ,once again, to the Grange family who donated all the funds raised by their Christmas Lights.
Designer Contracts generously donated lots of prizes for the Christmas Raffle.
We have been supported by Tesco who have donated craft supplies and raffle prizes.
We want to thank all the staff, families and those in the local community for the hard work which went in to making the Christmas Bazaar such a success.
The Grotto and visits by Santa were well received by school and local families. Thank you to everyone who helped.
Nisa and Making a Difference Locally have donated £850 towards upgrading our pool environment
Napa Automotive Parts had a collection box on their counter and have donated the funds raised.
Sponsorship events
Several people have completed various challenges and raised money through sponsorship.
Helen Murphy is running the 2026 London Marathon for Lime Academy Ravensbourne. Good Luck Helen!
In May 2025 Kaspar ran the Hackney Half Marathon raising money for Ravensbourne
Lime Academy Ravensbourne supports others
At Lime Academy Ravensbourne students and staff take part in various fundraising or charity days. Please check the school calendar of events and newsletters for further information.
This year so far we have raised money by Wearing it Pink for Breast Cancer Awareness Wearing Red for Comic Relief among others

Transport
Many of our pupils travel to school using school transport. For more information, or to find out if your child is eligible, please contact Havering Transport on 01708 441 287.
The service operates during term time, collecting children and young people from their homes or agreed collection points, ensuring they arrive on time and ready to learn. In the afternoon, they are collected at home time and returned safely back again.
All drivers and passenger assistants are specially trained to provide transport services for children and young people with SEN.
Eligibility is assessed by:
Before applying for travel assistance you must read the full criteria given in the policy document.
Distance
Safety of the route
Mobility needs
Types of Assistance
Assistance may be given by:
Travel training
Assistance in Future Years
You will be required to complete a new application every year. (April). Assistance with the costs of home to school/college transport cannot be guaranteed in future years.
Appeals
If a parent or carer is dissatisfied with the outcome of the application there is an appeals process which is outlined in the policy.
Important Information
If you currently receive transport support and your child’s circumstances have not changed, please submit a renewal request online.
Families whose circumstances have changed or who have not applied previously can submit a new application via the same link. Upon receipt, applications will be assessed, and you will be informed of the decision in writing via email.
Please be aware that the closing date for applications was Friday 24th May 2024. Please be aware that if an application was not received by this date, it will be assumed that your child no longer requires transport support. To avoid any disruption to your child’s education in September please submit an application ahead of this deadline. Late applications will be considered however arrangements may not be in place for the start of term.
Should you have any queries relating to travel assistance and/or eligibility, please contact CADTransport@Havering.gov.uk.
